source_row.stem: An adult client presents with gradual enlargement of the hands, feet, and facial features, along with joint pain, and a family member assumes these changes are probably just a normal, unremarkable part of getting older. The nurse should instead suspect:
source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"A normal, expected part of the aging process that would not usually prompt further hormonal evaluation, similar to what the family member is currently assuming","B":"Acromegaly, resulting from excess growth hormone in adulthood, rather than the ordinary aging the family member is currently assuming explains these gradual changes","C":"A simple allergic reaction, since gradual facial and extremity changes are thought by some to often reflect hypersensitivity, though this does not fit this presentation","D":"An unrelated musculoskeletal injury, since joint pain is thought by some to typically point to a local orthopedic cause, though this would not explain the other changes described"}}
source_row.rationale: Gradual enlargement of the hands, feet, and facial features (coarsening) along with joint pain in an adult are classic signs of acromegaly, caused by excess growth hormone, typically from a pituitary tumor.
source_row.source_name: Endocrine Society — Acromegaly Clinical Practice Guideline
